name: Urayuli
body:
Urayuli
CR 6

What seems like a shaggy pillar of fur lifts its arm up, its knuckles rugged from being dragged on the ground. Its eyes open, their bright glow enticing and soothing.

XP 2,400
N Large monstrous humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent; Perception +13

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 10, flat-footed 18 (+1 Dex, +9 natural, –1 size)
hp 66 (7d10+28)
Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +6; Resist cold 20

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +13 (1d8+7), 2 slams +14 (1d6+7)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft. (15 ft. with slam)
Special Attacks fascinating gaze

STATISTICS

Str 24, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 10
Base Atk +7; CMB +15; CMD 26
Feats Ability Focus (fascinating gaze), Great Fortitude, Power Attack, Toughness
Skills Perception +13, Stealth +11, Survival +8; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth
Languages Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Fascinating Gaze (Su)

Target is fascinated, 30 feet, Will DC 15 negates. Fascination lasts as long as the urayuli remains within 30 feet of the fascinated creature and spends a swift action each turn to maintain the gaze. Any action from the urayuli, including approach and attack, doesn’t count as threatening for the purpose of breaking the fascination. This is a mind-affecting effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold forests
Organization solitary, pair, or group (3-4)
Treasure standard

The urayuli are rare creatures, even more elusive than sasquatches and yeti, the humanoids most similar to them. They live only in large, cold forests and emerge mainly at night, preying on deer and elk. While their culture and society are unknown, if any exist, their behavior towards humanoids is often spoken about in hushed stories around campfires and in remote inns. According to those, they like to emerge into the fringes of their territories, waiting for intelligent prey to stumble into their domain, often children or careless hunters. They stand there, silently, nestled among trees and themselves looking like one, waiting for the victim to approach. Then, they open their large eyes, breaking the darkness with their dazzlingly bright light. They don’t have to pursue their victims, for anyone who meets an urayuli’s gaze lets it approach freely, only to be torn apart and eaten. According to some stories, many children meet an even worse fate, somehow being captured and turned into urayuli themselves by some strange process, though those rumors never found proof.

Urayuli are always silent when encountered, but some reports tell of them communicating between themselves with strange, high-pitched cries, resembling those of a loon. Cryptic information gleaned from druids and woodland creatures seem to suggest that the urayuli speak Sylvan, although there are no recorded cases of successful communication.

While their monstrous ambushes and killings of innocent victims would normally indicate evil beings, the rare paladins who set out to slay them and manage to find the beasts return confused, for the creatures don’t register as such. The reason for that is unknown and gaining such insight would most likely require a greater understanding of their lifestyle, an exceedingly difficult task given their rarity, reclusiveness and the danger they pose. An urayuli stands around 10 feet tall, its arms easily as long themselves. It weighs over 900 pounds and is covered in mounds of thick, shaggy, brownish fur that makes up much of its size.

This tall, bald man looks like a grotesque statue, horrifically scarred and thickened skin clinging to monstrously bulging muscles that somehow are no hindrance to his fluid movements and cat-like flexibility.
